verdict_rationale: A critical security invariant (authentication lockout) is violated on a reachable, session-less recovery command (P5-ADV-001). The candidate also fails the existing required verify:replication governance gate (P5-ADV-002) and does not enforce financial-integrity verification at the production restore boundary (P5-ADV-003), with four reproduced detector false negatives. Business-data ownership fencing, crash consistency, and fail-closed startup reconciliation were independently verified and are sound; they are not the basis for NO-GO. No finding was downgraded to reach this verdict.

independently_verified_invariants.invariant: Business-table fence blocks session-less raw SQL writes
independently_verified_invariants.evidence: audit_b1 positive control + candidate fence test (candidate-full-suite.txt)

independently_verified_invariants.invariant: No dual live ownership at startup
Pre-commit crash retains original financial data and durable fence
Completed crash is the sole durable success point
Startup rejects unknown recovery audit action
Startup rejects fence referencing a terminal operation
Startup rejects completed operation without result generation
Normal login lockout engages after five failures
Cloud rejects operation-identity payload reuse with CONFLICT
Cloud rejects stale restore generation with STALE_GENERATION

findings.title: Owner-resolution command has no brute-force lockout and grants an unlocked Owner session
findings.code_path: Tauri resolve_interrupted_recovery -> with_recovery_review_workspace -> verify_scope_readonly (no session) -> Workspace::resolve_interrupted_recovery -> recovery::resolve_interrupted. Reads owner retry_after and workspace_access.retry_after and honors an existing lockout, but on wrong password returns InvalidPassword without incrementing failed_attempts or setting retry_after (global or principal), and writes no session.unlocked audit. On success sets store.1 = Some(session) (unlocked Owner).
findings.attack_scenario: While the workspace is fenced (interrupted recovery after a crash), an attacker with local access to the registered, session-less Tauri command makes unlimited Owner-password guesses. The persistent 5-attempt/60s lockout that protects normal login is never engaged through this path; a correct guess yields a fully unlocked Owner session controlling all financial data.
findings.expected_invariant: Owner authentication must enforce the persistent brute-force lockout (failed_attempts increment, retry_after at threshold) on every authentication path, including recovery resolution; existing authentication safeguards must not be weakened.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: 25 consecutive wrong passwords all return InvalidPassword; local_principals and workspace_access failed_attempts/retry_after remain (0,0,0,0); the correct password then unlocks an Owner session and releases the fence.
findings.impact: Security: removal of the authentication rate-limit safeguard for the root Owner credential in the recovery scenario; unlimited online guessing (Argon2-bounded per attempt) plus full Owner session grant on success.
findings.recommended_remediation: Mirror login_at: increment global and principal failed_attempts, set retry_after at the threshold, audit failed resolution attempts, and add a regression test asserting lockout engages through the resolution path.

remediation.root_cause: Recovery Owner-password verification called Argon2 directly and never consulted or updated the durable workspace_access failure budget used by access::login_at, so the session-less command was an unlimited password oracle and a correct guess released the fence even during an active login lockout.
remediation.fix: resolve_interrupted_at shares the existing login lockout policy: active lockout (principal or global) returns RateLimited even with the correct password; failures durably increment failed_attempts (cap 5) and set retry_after=clock+60 with reset-to-1 after expiry; accounting is explicitly committed inside the IMMEDIATE writer transaction so it is restart-persistent and concurrency-safe; success clears the budget, audits session.unlocked, then releases the fence. StoreError::InvalidPassword preserved. No second password policy was introduced.
remediation.verification: cargo test --lib --locked --manifest-path packages/local-store/Cargo.toml recovery::remediation_tests => 6 passed / 0 failed, exit 0

independent_verification.result: IV001-IV006 drive the production API Workspace::resolve_interrupted_recovery. Candidate 0/6 (40 wrong passwords never rate-limited; correct password granted Ok(()) during would-be lockout; 32 concurrent never limited). Remediation 6/6: cap 5, RateLimited on correct password while locked, budget identical after reopen, shared with login, 28/32 concurrent limited, business write rejected by fence and login RecoveryActive.

findings.title: Existing verify:replication governance gate fails on the candidate
findings.code_path: node scripts/verify-replication.mjs compiles replication-cloud + mobile-contracts (succeeds), then asserts /const SCHEMA_VERSION: i64 = 12;/ against lib.rs (candidate is 13) -> AssertionError 'financial schema remains 12'. A later assertion requires desktopMain.includes('reset_sidecar_file'), which the candidate removed.
findings.attack_scenario: Not an attack; a regression. The candidate changed schema version and sidecar behavior but did not update the harness, so the project's required verification gate (npm run verify:replication, part of npm run verify) exits non-zero.
findings.expected_invariant: The candidate must pass the project's existing required governance/verification gates.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: REPLICATION_EXIT=1; AssertionError 'financial schema remains 12'. git diff baseline..candidate -- scripts/verify-replication.mjs is empty (harness unchanged). reset_sidecar_file occurrences in desktop main = 0.
findings.impact: Release-blocking governance regression; the candidate's verification suite fails. The audit did not weaken assertions.
findings.recommended_remediation: Update the harness to v13 invariants (schema 13; sidecar reset removed) without weakening assertions, and make verify:replication pass.

remediation.root_cause: The harness pinned financial schema 12 and asserted the presence of a sidecar-deletion reset path that v13 replaced with generation-keyed reset, so the required governance gate exited 1.
remediation.fix: Every obsolete assertion replaced with a meaningful v13 equivalent, none removed or weakened: schema pin 13 plus migrate_v13 and reconcile_startup wiring; sidecar-deletion presence inverted to absence plus on_restore / ack.on_restore(&generation) / stale-generation checks; added recovery-fencing and financial-module assertions. Full harness executed, not bypassed.
remediation.verification: node scripts/verify-replication.mjs => 120 checks passed exit 0 at this commit; 129 checks passed exit 0 after RULE 5 added dedup-contract checks

independent_verification.result: Official harness re-run independently: 129 checks, exit 0. Diff audit: exactly 2 obsolete assertions removed, 25 added; security/compatibility intent preserved by v13 equivalents.

findings.title: Financial-integrity verification is test-only and not enforced at the production restore boundary
findings.code_path: restore_owned T3 calls integrity() (PRAGMA cipher_integrity_check / integrity_check / foreign_key_check) only. financial_violations is referenced nowhere outside tests (repository-wide search). Comment: 'Deep financial-invariant verification is test-only by design.'
findings.attack_scenario: A backup whose financial data is logically invalid but structurally intact (e.g., logical on-disk corruption) passes validate() + integrity() and is imported and marked completed without financial verification.
findings.expected_invariant: Recovery must verify financial invariants at the restore boundary so it cannot silently commit invalid financial state.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: Production restore performs structural verification only; the deep financial verifier is test-only. End-to-end silent corruption was NOT demonstrated (schema validation requires the full trigger set; write-time triggers constrain normal data).
findings.reproduction_evidence: Source inspection (restore_owned T3; financial_violations cfg(test)); detector false negatives P5-ADV-004..007 reproduced in docs/reviews/phase5-adversarial-evidence/adversarial-all-12.txt
findings.impact: Financial-integrity guarantee is not enforced at the production boundary; the test oracle that underpins the claim is incomplete.
findings.recommended_remediation: Promote a hardened financial verifier out of #[cfg(test)] and run it inside the restore transaction before completion; reject backups that violate financial invariants.

remediation.root_cause: financial_violations had zero production callers; it existed only as a test oracle, so a restore could install a semantically corrupt ledger.
remediation.fix: New packages/local-store/src/recovery/financial.rs exposes violations() and verify(). verify() is called inside the single IMMEDIATE restore transaction after integrity() and before completion, raising StoreError::FinancialInconsistency; rejection rolls back the whole transaction, preserving the original database and fence. Desktop adapter maps the error to financial_inconsistency. The phase5 test oracle additionally calls the production verifier (additive).
remediation.verification: cargo test --lib --locked --manifest-path packages/local-store/Cargo.toml recovery::financial::financial_tests => 10 passed / 0 failed, exit 0 (includes end-to-end restore rejection and valid-backup-still-restores) | RULE 3 tests: rem_r3_detects_missing_postings_and_broken_stock_arithmetic, rem_r3_restore_rejects_financially_inconsistent_backup, rem_r3_tampered_backup_file_is_rejected_at_preview, rem_r3_valid_backup_still_restores

independent_verification.result: financial::verify confirmed inside the single IMMEDIATE restore tx after integrity() and before completion. Independent IVF10: corrupt backup rejected FinancialInconsistency, 2 original invoices intact, no fence left behind. IVF11 healthy backup restores clean.

findings.title: Verifier misses a deleted credit-sale entry (customer outstanding understated)
findings.code_path: Check 5: SELECT c.invoice_id FROM local_credit_entries c JOIN local_billing_ledger l ON l.invoice_id=c.invoice_id AND l.account='receivables' WHERE c.kind='sale' AND l.amount_paise<>c.amount_paise. INNER JOIN yields no row when the credit entry is deleted; billing ledger stays balanced.
findings.attack_scenario: On-disk corruption or tampering deletes a credit sale's local_credit_entries row; customer outstanding balance is understated and the verifier reports clean.
findings.expected_invariant: Every credit sale must have a matching credit entry; outstanding balance must reconcile.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: After DELETE of the kind='sale' entry, SUM(amount_paise) for the customer changes but financial_violations returns empty.
findings.impact: Financial: understated receivables/outstanding undetected by the integrity oracle.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add a check that every credit invoice has a corresponding credit entry (LEFT JOIN / NOT EXISTS), independent of ledger balance.

remediation.root_cause: The verifier checked aggregate balance only, which is unchanged when a credit-sale entry is deleted, so customer outstanding was understated without any violation.
remediation.fix: Credit invariant now requires credit sale <-> credit entry correspondence in BOTH directions, plus derived outstanding >= 0. Outstanding is recomputed from entries because local_customers has no stored balance column (documented limitation).
remediation.verification: rem_r3_detects_deleted_credit_sale_entry passes; financial suite 10 passed / 0 failed, exit 0

independent_verification.result: IVF01 independently reproduced: credit sale missing matching credit entry + customer outstanding is negative.

findings.title: Verifier misses tampered repayment/opening_due credit entries
findings.code_path: Check 5 filters c.kind='sale' only; repayment/opening_due/write_off entries are not cross-checked against the customer journal.
findings.attack_scenario: Tampering a repayment credit entry amount changes customer outstanding balance; the customer journal is untouched and balanced, so the verifier reports clean.
findings.expected_invariant: All credit entry kinds must reconcile with the customer journal/outstanding balance.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: UPDATE local_credit_entries SET amount_paise=amount_paise+5000 WHERE operation_id='cash-collection' leaves financial_violations empty.
findings.impact: Financial: outstanding balance manipulation undetected for non-sale credit kinds.
findings.recommended_remediation: Cross-check every credit kind against the customer journal and recompute outstanding balances.

remediation.root_cause: Tampered repayment/opening_due amounts preserved zero-sum journal balance, so the totals-only verifier accepted them.
remediation.fix: For non-sale credit entries the entry delta must equal the journal receivables movement, establishing the source-record to financial-consequence relationship rather than aggregate balance.
remediation.verification: rem_r3_detects_tampered_repayment_entry passes; financial suite 10 passed / 0 failed, exit 0

independent_verification.result: IVF02 independently reproduced: credit entry disagrees with customer journal.

findings.title: Verifier misses a balanced billing-ledger tamper versus invoice total
findings.code_path: Check 1 groups local_billing_ledger by invoice_id HAVING SUM(amount_paise)<>0. Shifting amount between revenue and cash keeps SUM=0; no check reconciles ledger legs to the invoice total.
findings.attack_scenario: A balanced tamper (revenue -100, cash +100) keeps the ledger zero-sum but the revenue leg no longer matches the invoice; the verifier reports clean.
findings.expected_invariant: Ledger postings must reconcile to the invoice total, not merely sum to zero.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: After the balanced shift, financial_violations returns empty while the revenue leg drifts from its original value.
findings.impact: Financial: revenue/cash misstatement undetected when balance is preserved.
findings.recommended_remediation: Reconcile ledger legs to the stored invoice total/tax and tender breakdown.

remediation.root_cause: A balanced revenue-to-cash shift kept SUM(postings)=0, so the totals-only verifier accepted a ledger that contradicted the invoice.
remediation.fix: Invoice-to-ledger invariants: postings exist, zero-sum, exactly one settlement leg matching total/tender/customer, revenue leg equals -subtotal, tax leg present iff tax>0, and subtotal+tax=total. The regression test asserts SUM is still 0 while the verifier rejects.
remediation.verification: rem_r3_detects_balanced_but_semantically_wrong_ledger passes; financial suite 10 passed / 0 failed, exit 0

independent_verification.result: IVF03 independently reproduced with ledger SUM confirmed still 0: settlement leg and revenue leg disagreements detected.

findings.title: Verifier misses a duplicated balanced retail journal
findings.code_path: local_retail_journal has sequence PK but no UNIQUE(operation_id,account). The verifier checks retail journal SUM per operation and outbox duplicates, but has no duplicate-journal check. Duplicating a balanced posting set keeps SUM=0.
findings.attack_scenario: On-disk duplication of a retail operation's postings double-counts revenue/cash while remaining zero-sum; the verifier reports clean.
findings.expected_invariant: Journal postings must be unique per operation/account; duplication must be detected.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: After duplicating the balanced set, financial_violations returns empty although a GROUP BY operation_id,account HAVING COUNT(*)>1 query detects duplicates.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add a duplicate-journal detector and a UNIQUE(operation_id,account) guard for local_retail_journal.

remediation.root_cause: Retail SALE postings were only checked relationally by amount, so duplicating both legs (cash 4250 -> 8500, receivables -4250 -> -8500) kept the operation zero-sum and the activity row intact: the derived independent test IVX01 found the sale case still open even after returns were covered.
remediation.fix: Sale operations additionally assert a cardinality invariant: exactly one cash leg and exactly one receivables leg iff the recorded cash payments are non-zero, and only those two accounts with no customer attribution. Duplicating a balanced sale pair (including the halved-amounts variant) therefore breaks the cardinality while legitimate multi-part returns, which repeat accounts by construction, stay accepted by the documented false-positive guard.
remediation.verification: fin01_duplicate_sale_journal_4250_scenario, fin02b_partial_missing_sale_journal, fin07b_duplicate_with_halved_amounts_keeps_sums and rem_r3_accepts_valid_history_including_multipart_returns all pass; full cargo test 262 passed / 0 failed, exit 0.

independent_verification.result: IVX01 (duplicate a SALE operation, cash 4250->8500 / receivables -4250->-8500, zero-sum preserved) is now detected by the sale-cardinality rule and rejected at the production restore boundary; the halved-amounts variant is covered by fin07b.

findings.title: Unfenced metadata tables writable via raw SQL while fenced (bounded)
findings.code_path: The engine fence triggers cover only the 40 FENCED_TABLES. workspace_access (lockout counters) and local_recovery_identity (business_id, generation) have no fence trigger; local_recovery_identity has no immutability trigger.
findings.attack_scenario: A session-less raw-SQL writer resets workspace_access lockout counters or tampers local_recovery_identity.generation while a recovery fence is active.
findings.expected_invariant: No unfenced writes that affect security/recovery identity during a live fence; no business-identity substitution.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: audit_b1: UPDATE workspace_access and UPDATE local_recovery_identity SET generation succeed while fenced; a business write (local_products) is rejected. audit_b2: business_id substitution is caught fail-closed at startup (RecoveryCorrupt).
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth gap: lockout reset and generation tamper between transactions; bounded by fail-closed startup for business substitution and by the writer lock during restore. Not a business-data ownership breach.
findings.recommended_remediation: Extend fencing/immutability to local_recovery_identity and workspace_access, or document and bound the metadata trust model; cross-check generation consistency.

remediation.rule: RULE 7 (metadata trust model, designed rather than patched)
remediation.root_cause: The fence triggers covered only the 40 FENCED_TABLES. workspace_access and local_recovery_identity had no trigger at all, so raw SQL with the SQLCipher key could, during a live fence, clear the shared 5-attempt/60s lockout, rewrite the restore generation and substitute business identity.
remediation.fix: Designed metadata trust model in V13_EXTENSION, all engine-level so every connection and every raw-SQL path is covered: (a) local_recovery_identity gets BEFORE INSERT (singleton + 64-hex shape + fenced), BEFORE DELETE (permanent) and BEFORE UPDATE (business_id immutable, generation shape, and FROZEN while a fence is live); (b) workspace_access gets BEFORE INSERT (singleton), BEFORE DELETE (permanent) and a fenced BEFORE UPDATE that refuses credential-policy changes and any weakening of the lockout while still permitting monotonic failure accounting, which is exactly what the P5-ADV-001 fix needs; (c) the two production code paths that legitimately write through these tables were re-ordered to respect the guards instead of the guards being weakened: resolve_interrupted_at now transitions the operation and releases the fence BEFORE clearing the shared budget, and restore_owned deletes the imported fence BEFORE rotating the generation. No validation was relaxed and no second password policy was introduced.
remediation.verification: cargo test --lib recovery:: => 78 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored, exit 0. New tests: recovery_metadata_is_immutable_while_fenced (replays every attack the audit used: budget reset, retry-window drop, credential swap, generation tamper, business_id substitution, identity delete — all refused, budget unchanged, accounting still monotonic); metadata_writes_are_allowed_once_the_fence_is_released (restore still rotates the generation and the Owner can still unlock); startup_rejects_malformed_recovery_identity. verify:local-schema => 110 checks passed including 11 new v13 guard attacks.

independent_verification.result: Re-ran the audit attack set against the new schema. All metadata tampering during a live fence is now refused by the engine (budget reset, retry-window drop, credential swap, workspace_access delete, generation tamper, business_id substitution, identity delete). The legitimate paths still work: an expired-window retry restarts the budget at 1, successful resolution releases the fence and clears the budget, and a full restore still rotates the generation.

findings.title: Cloud in-memory dedup is cross-generation while durable Postgres dedup is per-generation
findings.code_path: ingest.ts dedups by `${businessId}|${operationId}` (cross-generation). postgres.ts dedups by (business_id, restore_generation, stream, operation_id) (SQL UNIQUE line 50). After a restore rotates the generation, Postgres would not dedup against the prior generation's events.
findings.attack_scenario: Post-restore re-publication of the same operationId under a new generation is deduped in-memory (duplicate=true) but could be re-projected by the Postgres path; journal/credit projection idempotency is not guaranteed by the per-generation key.
findings.expected_invariant: Consistent dedup semantics across reference and durable paths; no double-projection of financial events after restore.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: Probe: gen-2 redelivery of a gen-1 operation returns duplicate=true (in-memory). Postgres per-generation key confirmed by source/SQL; not executed (no Postgres instance).
findings.impact: Potential cloud-side double-projection of financial events after restore; requires production-path verification.
findings.recommended_remediation: Align dedup semantics and verify projection idempotency for journals/credits across in-memory and Postgres paths.

remediation.root_cause: In-memory dedup was keyed businessId|operationId (cross-generation) while durable Postgres dedup included restore_generation. Separately, the in-memory duplicate branch returned early without advancing the new generation stream head, so after a restore the first genuinely new operation was rejected GAP and could never be published.
remediation.fix: Decision: cross-generation dedup is intentional and required; a restore generation is a transport epoch, not business identity, and bumpCustomer applies a delta so re-projection would double-count outstanding. postgres.ts duplicate lookup drops restore_generation and selects the earliest event, advances the current generation head under FOR UPDATE when contiguous, and inserts a per-generation ack ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. ingest.ts advances the head when a duplicate is exactly last+1 via clone/adopt. Retries of a seen sequence stay idempotent with the original cursor. Full 9-clause contract documented.
remediation.verification: Durable path executed on real PostgreSQL 16.2: verify:replication-postgres => 79 checks passed. In-memory contract re-executed after the P5-NEW-006 key correction: verify:replication => 139 checks passed.

independent_verification.result: DURABLE PATH NOW VERIFIED ON REAL POSTGRESQL 16.2 (previously BLOCKED). 36/36 independent assertions incl. 4-way concurrent duplicate ingestion (1 event row, same cursor), sequence race (exactly 1 winner, 3 DUPLICATE_SEQUENCE, head advances once), and rollback (no partial event/ack, head unchanged). Candidate proven defective on the same server: full ordered outbox replay doubled outstanding 5000->10000 with duplicate event rows; remediation preserved 5000 with all duplicates. In-memory contract 18/18.

findings.title: owner_token and generation format are not validated
findings.code_path: owner_token/generation are produced by random_id() (hex) but neither admission nor reconciliation validates their format/length; pairing checks assume well-formed values.
findings.attack_scenario: A tampered-but-nonempty token/generation that still satisfies fence pairing is not rejected on format alone.
findings.expected_invariant: Recovery identity tokens/generations should be validated for expected format.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: No format validation observed in admit or reconcile_startup (source inspection).
findings.impact: Low; values are internal and pairing-checked.
findings.recommended_remediation: Validate token/generation format (length/charset) at admission and reconciliation.

remediation.root_cause: random_id() emits 64 lowercase hex, but no consumer validated the shape, so a tampered-but-nonempty generation/business identity was accepted at admission and passed startup reconciliation as long as it satisfied the pairing checks.
remediation.fix: is_hex64() added and enforced at every recovery boundary: generation() consumers in admit(), the transition() completion generation, restore_owned() before execution, and reconcile_startup() for business_id, the live generation, every operation_id and every completed result_generation. reconcile_startup also now requires the newest completed result_generation to equal the live generation, so a rollback or a forged completion cannot masquerade as clean. The same shape is enforced in SQL by the two new local_recovery_identity triggers, so it holds for raw writes too. Malformed metadata returns StoreError::RecoveryCorrupt (fail closed, original files preserved).
remediation.verification: startup_rejects_malformed_recovery_identity covers the audit's exact accepted values ("short", "zzzz", "'; DROP TABLE x; --", "") plus non-hex/short business identities and a malformed or mismatched completed result_generation — every one now returns RecoveryCorrupt. verify:local-schema asserts the engine refuses a non-hex and a shortened generation at INSERT/UPDATE.

independent_verification.result: All four malformed generations the audit accepted now return RecoveryCorrupt at Store::open, as do malformed business identities and malformed/mismatched completed result generations.

findings.title: clippy -D warnings yields pre-existing style lints; plain gate passes
findings.code_path: cargo clippy --all-targets (plain) exits 0 with 17 lib warnings (19 in test cfg). Adding -D warnings promotes them to errors (exit 101): too_many_arguments, needless_borrow, type_complexity, redundant_pattern_matching, manual RangeInclusive contains.
findings.attack_scenario: Not a security defect; style lints, predominantly pre-existing baseline code.
findings.recommended_remediation: Optionally address style lints; not release-blocking.

remediation.root_cause: 19 clippy lints surfaced under `-D warnings` (11 needless_borrow in billing.rs, unneeded_wildcard_pattern in payments.rs, type_complexity in customers.rs, four too_many_arguments, two test idioms) plus 2 ESLint unused-variable warnings.
remediation.fix: Fixed rather than silenced wherever the lint was right: needless borrows removed, the redundant wildcard pattern collapsed, a CustomerRow type alias introduced, and the two test idioms rewritten. Four too_many_arguments sites (restore_backup, customers::entry, payments::return_invoice, payments::csv_row) keep their explicit argument lists with a documented #[allow] because each argument is a distinct security- or money-bearing fact and a wrapper struct would only lengthen their lifetime. The two ESLint findings were dead code (an unused parameter and an unused import) and were removed.
remediation.verification: cargo clippy --all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings => exit 0 (was exit 101 with 19 warnings). cargo fmt --check => exit 0. npm run lint => exit 0 with 0 warnings (was exit 0 with 2 warnings).

independent_verification.result: clippy -D warnings exit 0 and ESLint 0 warnings, both re-executed after the change.

findings.title: Restore-boundary verifier rejects every legitimate split cash+credit retail sale and misses a deleted split-credit entry
findings.code_path: A split retail sale posts cash/UPI/card parts through payments::invoice_posted and books ONLY the credit part as customer debt via customers::post_split_credit, whose entry carries invoice_id=invoice and kind=sale with amount = credit parts (< invoice total). The reverse-direction rule required json_extract(payload,'$.tender')='credit' AND totalPaise = entry amount, which no split sale satisfies. Because that rule never looked at retail invoices, deleting the split-credit entry was also undetected.
findings.attack_scenario: A shop that sells partly on khata cannot restore its own backup at all (availability defect), and a backup whose split-credit entry was lost silently understates customer outstanding.
findings.expected_invariant: A split cash+credit retail sale must restore successfully, and its credit entry must be reconciled exactly once in both directions.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: sales-by-sale: legitimate split sale => FinancialInconsistency on restore; deleted split-credit entry => violations()==[] on the candidate.
findings.impact: Blocks restore for a normal khata workflow; hides lost receivable.
findings.recommended_remediation: Accept tender=credit OR (tender=retail AND credit parts = entry amount AND customer matches); add the retail-direction cardinality and amount rules.

remediation.root_cause: The credit-entry reverse rule assumed every sale entry belongs to a tender=credit invoice, which is false for split retail sales.
remediation.fix: The reverse rule now accepts the split form as well (retail tender, credit parts equal to the entry amount, same customer). Two new forward rules make it bidirectional: a retail invoice must have exactly one kind=sale entry iff its credit parts are non-zero, and that entry must equal the recorded credit parts for the invoice customer. No rule was loosened: the tender=credit form and all amount/customer equalities are still required.
remediation.verification: p5_new_001_split_cash_credit_sale_is_accepted (accepted, then a real export/preview/restore round trip succeeds) and p5_new_001_deleted_split_credit_entry_is_detected both pass; the whole financial suite is 16 passed / 0 failed, exit 0.

independent_verification.result: False positive reproduced and removed; the deletion attack is now reported as "retail split credit is not exactly one credit entry" and verify() returns FinancialInconsistency.

findings.title: Restore-boundary verifier rejects legitimate repeated-product invoice lines and cannot see duplicate-line under-deduction
findings.code_path: billing::post_into aggregates requested quantity per product (`quantities` BTreeMap) and writes ONE local_invoice_stock row per product, while the invoice payload keeps every line. The verifier compared each payload line against a stock movement, so two lines of the same product never matched.
findings.attack_scenario: Any invoice that bills the same product on two lines cannot be restored; a movement matching only one of the lines hides an under-deducted stock quantity.
findings.expected_invariant: SUM(quantity_milli per product) in the payload must equal the stock movement(s) for that product, both directions.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: legitimate two-line invoice => FinancialInconsistency; movement cut to one line => violations()==[] on the candidate.
findings.impact: Blocks restore for a normal basket; hides inventory corruption.
findings.recommended_remediation: Aggregate payload lines by (invoice, product) before comparing, and compare the aggregate to SUM(stock movements).

remediation.root_cause: The comparison was line-oriented while the writer is product-oriented.
remediation.fix: Both directions rewritten to aggregate: GROUP BY (invoice, productId) with SUM(quantityMilli) compared to COALESCE(SUM(local_invoice_stock.quantity_milli),0), and a movement for an unbilled product is still rejected. The per-movement arithmetic check (after = before - quantity) and non-negative stock checks are unchanged.
remediation.verification: p5_new_002_repeated_product_lines_are_accepted (proves the real writer emits one aggregated movement of 1000) and p5_new_002_duplicate_line_under_deduction_is_detected both pass; financial suite 16 passed / 0 failed, exit 0.

independent_verification.result: Both the false positive and the blind spot are closed; the one pre-existing test that asserted the old label was updated to the new label without weakening its assertion.

findings.title: Non-sale credit entries were only checked when a journal row existed, and kind=return entries had no bilateral verification
findings.code_path: The non-sale rule was guarded by EXISTS(local_customer_journal ...), so a DELETED journal row skipped the comparison entirely. kind=return entries (written by customers::invoice_return from local_retail_return_parts.debt) were not verified against the return record or the retail journal at all.
findings.attack_scenario: Delete a repayment journal leg, or delete/inflate a return debt entry, and the restore boundary still reports clean data.
findings.expected_invariant: Every journal-backed credit entry must equal its journal receivables leg, and every return must reconcile with its recorded debt in both directions.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: deleted journal row => violations()==[]; inconsistent return debt => violations()==[] on the candidate.
findings.impact: Silent understatement of collected cash or of cancelled debt.
findings.recommended_remediation: Require the journal row unconditionally (COALESCE to 0) and verify returns against local_retail_return_parts.debt and the attributed retail journal leg in both directions.

remediation.root_cause: A conditional guard turned a required relationship into an optional one.
remediation.fix: The guard is gone: kind IN (repayment, opening_due, write_off, reversal, link_in, link_out) must match COALESCE(SUM(journal receivables),0) exactly, and a new rule requires each linked entry to have an offsetting counterpart on a different customer. Two new rules verify kind=return against SUM(local_retail_return_parts.debt) in both directions and against the customer-attributed retail journal receivables leg.
remediation.verification: p5_new_003_deleted_journal_row_behind_a_credit_entry_is_detected and p5_new_003_credit_return_entry_must_match_the_return_record (which first proves a real credit refund is ACCEPTED, then deletes the debt entry and requires detection) both pass.

independent_verification.result: The false-negative is closed; the false-positive guard for legitimate credit refunds passes in the same run.

findings.title: verify:local-schema fails on schema v13 and the committed fingerprint still described schema 12
findings.code_path: The verifier replayed only `fn migrate` bodies. Schema 13 is applied by `recovery::migrate_v13` with the DDL inline in V13_EXTENSION plus a per-FENCED_TABLES trigger loop, so it was never replayed: user_version stayed 12 against SCHEMA_VERSION 13, and the structural fingerprint and guard attacks described the old schema.
findings.attack_scenario: A required governance gate (part of npm run verify) fails on the branch, and the schema fingerprint — the mechanism that catches a silently removed guard — was blind to every v13 guard.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: npm run verify:local-schema exit 1 with 2/92 failures on the baseline commit.
findings.expected_invariant: The schema verifier must replay and fingerprint the CURRENT schema, and every guard it ships must be attacked.
findings.reproduction_evidence: baseline gate run: "user_version is 12, crate SCHEMA_VERSION is 13" and "legacy v4 database upgrades to schema 13"
findings.impact: Release-blocking governance regression plus loss of the guard-regression detector for v13.
findings.recommended_remediation: Replay migrate_v13 (V13_EXTENSION + the FENCED_TABLES loop), refresh the fingerprint, and add v13 guard attacks.

remediation.root_cause: The loader discovered migrations by the literal name `migrate`, so a version-step with another name was invisible to it.
remediation.fix: load_migrations() now also resolves `recovery::migrate_v13`: it extracts the V13_EXTENSION const, expands the per-FENCED_TABLES barrier loop, and asserts the lib.rs step order ends with migrate_v13. The fingerprint was regenerated from the real engine (pure additions: 2 tables, 12 metadata triggers, 120 barrier triggers, no table shape change and no trigger removed). Eleven v13 guard attacks were added, and the seeded database now includes the singleton workspace_access row the v3 migration creates.
remediation.verification: npm run verify:local-schema => all 110 schema checks passed, exit 0 (baseline: exit 1).

independent_verification.result: The gate now fails loudly if a future v13 guard is removed, because the fingerprint contains the new tables and every metadata/barrier trigger.

findings.title: The PostgreSQL replication migration is not re-runnable
findings.code_path: Every object used a bare CREATE (tables, index, view, policies). applyReplicationMigration simply executes the file, so a retried deploy or a second call against an already-migrated database aborts.
findings.attack_scenario: A deploy retry, a rolled-forward environment, or any second apply of the migration fails partway, leaving the operator to hand-repair the schema.
findings.expected_invariant: Applying the migration twice must be a no-op and must leave exactly one of every object.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: Round 1 OK, round 2 fails 42P07 relation "businesses" already exists.
findings.impact: Operational: recovery from a failed deploy requires manual DBA intervention.
findings.recommended_remediation: Make every statement idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE OR REPLACE / existence-guarded policies).

remediation.root_cause: Idempotency was never a requirement for this file.
remediation.fix: Tables -> CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; index -> IF NOT EXISTS; function and view -> CREATE OR REPLACE; the seven policies -> individual DO blocks guarded by pg_policies. ALTER/GRANT/REVOKE are already repeatable. No policy predicate, CHECK constraint, grant or row-level-security setting was changed.
remediation.verification: Executed on a real PostgreSQL 16.2 server: three consecutive applies all succeed with a stable object count (11 tables, 7 policies, 8 RLS tables, 14 indexes, 1 view). verify:replication-postgres => 79 checks passed and verify:replication-native-https => 123 checks passed against that same server.

independent_verification.result: Before/after reproduced on the same server in the same session; the candidate fails on round 2, the fixed file succeeds on rounds 1-3.

findings.title: Cloud ingest rejects the second envelope of every real desktop retail sale because operation identity omits the stream
findings.code_path: A desktop retail sale writes ONE operationId to two outboxes: local_retail_outbox (stream=retail) and local_billing_outbox (stream=billing) — CheckoutPanel.tsx reuses request.operationId for the retail action, payments.rs::post_retail stores it, and replication_matrix_tests.rs proves the native export emits both (bill-cash-upi is billing seq 5 and retail seq 3). PostgreSQL scopes identity as (business_id, restore_generation, stream, operation_id) and postgres.ts dedups with stream, but store.ts and ingest.ts keyed store.byOperation by `${businessId}|${operationId}` and hydrateFromPostgres did the same.
findings.attack_scenario: Every genuine retail sale paid by UPI, card, cash+UPI, cash+card or cash+credit fails to replicate: the first (retail) envelope commits, then the billing envelope of the SAME commit is matched against the retail payload, its payloadSha256 differs, and ingest throws CONFLICT. The sale never reaches the cloud projection, so the shop reports and khata silently diverge from the PC. Separately, hydrateFromPostgres overwrites the retail entry with the billing entry, so post-restart duplicate detection compares a billing payload with a retail envelope.
findings.expected_invariant: Operation identity must be (business, stream, operation), the same key the durable schema uses; two envelopes of one commit must both commit and each retry must stay idempotent with its own cursor.
findings.actual_observed_behavior: Candidate: retail envelope accepted, billing envelope => ReplicationError CONFLICT; after hydration only one byOperation entry exists for the shared id; the native SQLCipher export of seven real sales contains exactly these shared ids and cannot be replicated.
findings.impact: Critical: silent loss of the cloud copy of the majority of real retail sales, and a false CONFLICT that a retrying publisher cannot resolve. It was masked because the synthetic fixtures used distinct bill-N and sale-N ids.
findings.recommended_remediation: Put the stream into the in-memory operation key everywhere (ingest, clone, hydration) and add a real shared-id fixture.

remediation.root_cause: The in-memory dedup key was narrower than the durable key: it dropped the stream dimension that the native outboxes genuinely use.
remediation.fix: CloudStore.operationKey(businessId, stream, operationId) is now the single source of the identity string; ingestEnvelope uses it for both lookup and insert, clone() rebuilds byOperation from the copy's own event log with it, and hydrateFromPostgres derives it from the stored row stream. The cross-generation dedup decision of P5-ADV-009 is unchanged: restore_generation is still deliberately excluded. The contract document and the harness source assertion were updated to the corrected identity, and a real shared-id fixture was added to both the in-memory and the durable suites.
remediation.verification: In-memory: verify:replication => 139 checks passed, exit 0, including both envelopes committing, both retries returning their own original cursor, the clone preserving both, and a changed payload still CONFLICT. Durable on real PostgreSQL 16.2: verify:replication-postgres => 79 checks passed, including two event rows for the shared id, independent cursors, hydration keeping both stream identities and the same-payload-conflict rejection. Native: verify:replication-native-https => 123 checks passed over the real SQLCipher export that contains shared ids.

independent_verification.result: Each claim re-executed: candidate CONFLICT vs fixed acceptance on the in-memory path; candidate hydration collapse vs fixed two-key hydration on real PostgreSQL; idempotency, conflict rejection and cross-generation dedup all still hold.
